title: Graph basics and BFS
objective: Explore a graph in rings of distance with a queue, finding the fewest steps to every place.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): graph representations and breadth-first search

simplifies: Every link counts as one step. When links have different lengths (distances, costs), BFS no longer gives shortest routes; Dijkstra does.

quiz.prompt: Why does BFS find the fewest steps?

options.text: It finishes everything 1 step away before anything 2 steps away, and so on
options.explanation: Right. The queue keeps the rings in order, so a place is first reached by a shortest route.
It reaches each place once and never tries the rest.

options.text: It picks the shortest link each time
options.explanation: All links are equal here; the queue order is what matters.
Right. Places are explored in the order they were found.
A stack would dive deep first: that is DFS.
